# O30 — Open-entry scenic surround, person on the ground

This is the low-complexity alternative if an occupied inflatable and its support
cannot satisfy the budget or product requirements. It changes the experience:
the person stands/sits on an independently supported surface inside an open
scenic surround. It is not a suspended zorb and is not the selected baseline.

1. Andrew decides whether this experience is acceptable as a fallback; record
   that choice before buying O30-only parts.
2. Mark an approximately 3 m scenic envelope and generous open entrance, with
   the person and accessible circulation on the ground. Do not close the
   entrance with a front leg, base rail, taut line or cable.
3. Test small samples of diffusing fabric/mesh with the intended LED or projector
   in representative darkness. Record transmission, spill, seams and view angles.
4. Reviewer/fabricator defines a scenery-only frame, joints, feet, edges and
   venue-accepted wind restraint. The surface area still creates wind load.
5. Obtain quotes for selected material, panels, fasteners, ground protection,
   wiring, review and transport; sum only O30 rows and chosen modules.
6. Fabricate the accepted frame, inspect joints/edges and dry-assemble it. Label
   the open front; provide independent supported seating if seating is selected.
7. Fit removable panels with the reviewed attachment method and required
   material documentation. Keep vented/open areas and the entry route intact.
8. Install selected light/control equipment with rear/side cables and protection;
   test switching, electrical load and participant sightlines.
9. Rehearse entry, stopping the show and rapid closure/packing with the crew.
10. Obtain venue acceptance, install, operate and strike under the field plan.

**BOM:** O30 scenery rows + common operations/electrical + one light module.
Exclude sphere, blower, inflatable repair kit, cradle, webbing and aerial rig.
The published surround allocation is a planning range, not a purchasing quote.
